new_statements.quote: Phonological words in Bahnaric may be mono- or disyllabic, with the latter generally treated as sesquisyllablic (iambic stress). [...] The vowels in stressed and unstressed syllables differ in their phonological status. Typically only a single non-contrastive vowel, usually schwa or conditioned variant, and a reduced consonant inventory occur in unstressed syllables, while the main syllables carry the full and rather large range of contrastive vowels and consonants. [...] Like most Austroasiatic languages, the Bahnaric languages are not tonal, but many—such as Sedang—contrast two phonation types (e.g. most if not all North Bahnaric languages contrast breathy versus modal voice, Sedang oddly contrasts creaky versus modal voice).
new_statements.citation: Cheeseman, Nathaniel, Jennifer Herington & Paul Sidwell. 2013. Bahnaric linguistic bibliography with selected annotations. Mon-Khmer Studies 42: xxxiv-lxvii. [section 3 'General linguistic features of Bahnaric languages', p. xxxvii] (A's work 1, re-listed by the checker for a branch-level passage A did not report)
new_statements.locator: section 3 'General linguistic features of Bahnaric languages', p. xxxvii (held the text)
new_statements.relation_note: For Bahnaric generally: phonological words are mono- or disyllabic, disyllables being sesquisyllabic with iambic stress (reduced presyllable + stressed main syllable, schwa-type vowel and reduced consonant inventory in the unstressed syllable); Bahnaric languages are not tonal; most if not all North Bahnaric languages contrast breathy vs modal register (Sedang creaky vs modal). Nothing specific to Halang Doan.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Genus-level: in disyllabic (sesquisyllabic) words stress falls on the final, main syllable; the presyllable is unstressed and reduced; no lexical tone; register (phonation) contrast typical of North Bahnaric. Stated for Bahnaric as a branch, not for Halang Doan.
new_statements.exceptions: none (branch-level generalisation; Sedang's creaky/modal register noted as odd)
new_statements.identity_note: BRANCH-LEVEL statement, not a Halang Doan description: the passage characterises 'Bahnaric languages' as a whole (the work's declared ISO scope, p. xxxiv, includes hld) and illustrates with Sedang (Smith 1979); the work contains no Halang Doan/Duan form or datum anywhere (hld only in the ISO list and the language-index row). Usable at most as a genus-level default by membership; it is not a languoid-level record and should not be counted as a verified statement for hala1253.
